title: Find social media profiles by username
description: Type one username, or several, and get every public profile that uses it. Every run checks all 999 sites the scanner knows and returns every detail it can read. Only the username is needed; the rest narrows the search.

username.title: Username
username.description: The handle to look up, for example elonmusk. You can paste @elonmusk or a profile link such as twitter.com/elonmusk, we take the handle out of it. Several at once: separate them with commas. If you paste an email address, we search the part before the @ and point you to the email tool.

usernames.title: More usernames (bulk)
usernames.description: One handle per line for bulk checks, up to 25 per run. Each username is scanned on its own: all 999 sites take about 3 minutes per username, so for more than 8 usernames lower 'How many sites to check' or raise the time limit.

top.title: How many sites to check
top.description: All 999 sites by default, the deepest scan possible, about 3 minutes per username. Lower it to check only the most popular N sites: 100 sites take about 30 seconds.
top.sectionDescription: Leave these empty to check the most popular sites. Set one or more to narrow the search; filters combine.

websites.title: Only these sites
websites.description: Check only the sites you name, by domain: github.com, reddit.com, instagram.com. A partial name like github also works. Any of the 999 sites in the list is accepted; the run tells you if a name is not on it. When set, 'How many sites to check' is ignored.

siteType.title: Only this category
siteType.description: Restrict the search to one kind of site. The counts show how many sites are in each category. Combine with 'How many sites to check' to take the most popular ones in that category.

countries.title: Only sites from these countries
countries.description: Where the site is based, not where the person lives. Most sites in the list are American or Indian; pick a country only when you know the person uses local platforms.

filter.title: Which matches to keep
filter.description: How sure a match must be before it is reported. Confident = the site answered exactly as a real profile does (100% match). Possible = 50 to 99%, likely but worth a manual look; some sites answer with a normal page for any handle. The default keeps both; choose confident-only for the cleanest list, or everything to include weak guesses below 50%.
enumTitles: Confident and possible matches (50% and up, recommended)
filter.sectionDescription: What each row should carry. Every found profile is one row, plus one summary row per run.

metadata.title: Add page details (title, description, image, language)
metadata.description: Reads each confident profile page for its meta tags (title, description, image, type) and detects the page language. On by default.

extract.title: Pull out emails, links and other patterns
extract.description: Scans each found profile page for email addresses, links and similar patterns and adds them to the row. Slower, and most sites show none without login.

timeout.title: Time limit (seconds)
timeout.description: The whole run stops after this many seconds (maximum 3600). Usernames that could not start in time are listed in the summary instead of failing the run. One username on all 999 sites needs about 3 minutes.
